genxml.title: REX3 raster engine (Indy and Indigo2 graphics)
genxml.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header
genxml.doc: Register file of the REX3 chip. Offsets are bytes from the REX3 base, which is 0xf0000 from the board base the public drivers map. Every register is 32 bits wide. The draw registers can be written at their own offset (the value is stored) or at the same offset plus GO_OFFSET (the value is stored and the primitive the latched draw mode describes is started); the configuration registers further up the map have the same pair, the same distance apart. Names and offsets are the ones the public Linux and NetBSD Newport headers declare, which agree where both define a register. Where only Linux declares a register the grade is inferred and the entry says so, unless a reading already in this repository confirms the offset. The drivers show what software writes and expects, not what the chip does with it: a role given from a name alone is marked inferred in the entry. Reset values are not given: no source states one. Nothing was measured on a board.

struct.name: DRAWMODE1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_DRAWMODE1
struct.doc: Draw mode word 1: the plane group and depth a draw writes, the host-port packing (RWPACKED, HOSTDEPTH, RWDOUBLE, SWAPENDIAN, written up in devices/rex3/host-pixels.md), the compare, dither, blend and logic-operation state. Every bit and value here is named at the same position in both headers (two value names differ, noted on the enums); what a bit does is graded per field, and only the host-port fields have a reading beyond the name.

struct.name: DRAWMODE0
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_DRAWMODE0
struct.doc: Draw mode word 0, the command register: the opcode, the addressing mode and the per-primitive option bits. NetBSD's console code draws with opcode draw in block mode and copies with scr2scr; the host-pixel paths are in devices/rex3/host-pixels.md. Bit positions and names are the same in both headers, except that only Linux names addressing modes 5 and 6. What each option bit does is not read beyond its name, except where the field says otherwise.

struct.name: LSMODE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_LSMODE
struct.doc: Line-stipple mode word. Its field layout is in neither header, so none is given here.

struct.name: LSPATTERN
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_LSPATTERN
struct.doc: Line-stipple pattern word.

struct.name: LSPATSAVE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_LSPATSAVE
struct.doc: Backup copy of the stipple pattern, named save by Linux's comment (a backup of the pattern).

struct.name: ZPATTERN
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_ZPATTERN
struct.doc: Per-pixel pattern word; NetBSD's glyph path writes it at the GO alias once per row, with the row's glyph bits.

struct.name: COLORBACK
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_COLORBACK
struct.doc: Background colour. NetBSD stores the glyph background colour index here.

struct.name: COLORVRAM
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_COLORVRAM
struct.doc: Clear colour for the fast VRAM clear (Linux comment); NetBSD's rectangle fill writes the colour here with FASTCLEAR set.

struct.name: ALPHAREF
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_ALPHAREF
struct.doc: Reference alpha value for the alpha-function compare (Linux comment).

struct.name: STALL0
struct.from: NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_STALL0; Linux Newport framebuffer header leaves the word undeclared
struct.doc: NetBSD names this word a stall register and its comment says a write waits until the engine is idle. Linux declares only a pad here. Role inferred from NetBSD's name and comment; neither driver writes it.

struct.name: SMASK0X
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK0X
struct.doc: Screen mask 0, x extent: a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment says min and max, 16.16). Which half is which is not read.

struct.name: SMASK0Y
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK0Y
struct.doc: Screen mask 0, y extent, packed as SMASK0X.

struct.name: SETUP
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SETUP
struct.doc: Setup trigger. Both headers declare it; neither drives it in the console paths read. Linux names it with a leading underscore.

struct.name: STEPZ
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member _stepz
struct.doc: Linux declares a word here named stepz. Single source; role unknown beyond the name.

struct.name: LSRESTORE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member _lsrestore
struct.doc: Linux declares it, next to LSPATSAVE; the name reads as restoring the stipple state. Single source; role inferred from the name only.

struct.name: LSSAVE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member _lssave
struct.doc: Linux declares it next to LSRESTORE; the name reads as saving the stipple state. Single source; role inferred from the name only.

struct.name: XSTART
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_XSTART, member _xstart; NetBSD sgimips Newport driver board probe
struct.doc: Current x start of the primitive, integer and fraction combined. NetBSD's board probe writes 0x12345678 to XSTARTI and expects this register to read the low 16 bits of that shifted left by PROBE_XSTART_SHIFT. A qtest can discriminate: write 0x12345678 to XSTARTI and expect 0x02b3c000 from XSTART.

struct.name: YSTART
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member _ystart
struct.doc: Current y start, counterpart of XSTART. Single source (the name pairs it with XSTART).

struct.name: XEND
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member _xend
struct.doc: Current x end point. Single source.

struct.name: YEND
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member _yend
struct.doc: Current y end point. Single source.

struct.name: XSAVE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member xsave
struct.doc: Copy of the integer x start for block addressing, from the Linux comment (a copy of xstart for block mode). Single source.

struct.name: XYMOVE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_XYMOVE
struct.doc: Signed x and y offset applied for relative operations such as a screen copy (Linux comment: an offset from xstart, ystart). NetBSD packs x in bits 31:16 and y in bits 15:0 and, for a copy, stores the destination minus the source.

struct.name: BRESD
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member bresd
struct.doc: Bresenham line decision term (name only). Single source.

struct.name: BRESS1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member bress1
struct.doc: Bresenham line term S1 (name only). Single source.

struct.name: BRESOCTINC1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member bresoctinc1; the offset also matches the host-pixel reading in devices/rex3/host-pixels.md
struct.doc: Bresenham octant and first increment. The host-pixel image put clears it before storing pixel words (devices/rex3/host-pixels.md).

struct.name: XSTARTF
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member xstartf
struct.doc: Start x as a float-format value (Linux types it as a float or word union). Single source.

struct.name: YSTARTF
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member ystartf

struct.name: YENDF
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member yendf
struct.doc: End y, same layout as XSTARTF. Single source.

struct.name: XSTARTI
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_XSTARTI; NetBSD sgimips Newport driver board probe
struct.doc: Start x as an integer. NetBSD's board probe writes 0x12345678 here and reads XSTART; see that register.

struct.name: XENDF1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member xendf1
struct.doc: A second end-x word Linux declares (named xendf1). Single source; MAME's model reads this offset as a copy of the XENDF word, which is a model, not evidence.

struct.name: XYSTARTI
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_XYSTARTI
struct.doc: Start x and y as one packed integer word: x in bits 31:16, y in bits 15:0 (NetBSD packs x << 16 | y; devices/rex3/host-pixels.md records the image put writing it this way).

struct.name: XYENDI
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_XYENDI
struct.doc: End x and y as one packed integer word, packed as XYSTARTI.

struct.name: XSTARTENDI
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member xstartendi
struct.doc: Start and end x as integers in one word (name only). Single source.

struct.doc: Red (or colour-index) colour, full state. Named and placed by Linux alone, whose comment calls the group iterators with full state for a context switch. Single source; the shading arithmetic is not read.

struct.name: WRMASK
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_WRMASK
struct.doc: Plane write mask. NetBSD stores 0xffffffff for a fill and 0xff when drawing 8-bit glyphs.

struct.name: COLORI
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_COLORI
struct.doc: Packed integer colour. NetBSD stores the glyph foreground colour index here.

struct.name: COLORX
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member colorx
struct.doc: Linux declares a colour word here named colorx. Single source; role unknown beyond the name.

struct.name: SLOPERED1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member slopered1
struct.doc: Linux declares a second red slope word here. Single source; role unknown beyond the name.

struct.name: HOSTRW0
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_HOSTRW0
struct.doc: Host data port, most significant word (devices/rex3/host-pixels.md for the packing at each depth and the GO alias used for pixel stores).

struct.name: HOSTRW1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_HOSTRW1
struct.doc: Host data port, least significant word; used only for 64-bit transfers (devices/rex3/host-pixels.md).

struct.name: DCBMODE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_DCBMODE
struct.doc: Display control bus mode: the data width, the slave address and register select, the acknowledge type and the chip-select timing for the next DCBDATA transfer. The two headers define the same bit positions and names. devices/rex3/byte-lanes.md records how the data bytes travel.

struct.name: DCBDATA0
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_DCBDATA0
struct.doc: Display bus data, most significant word. Linux accesses it as a word, as halfword 1 at +2 and as byte 3 at +3 depending on DATAWIDTH; NetBSD packs the first byte in bits 31:24 (devices/rex3/byte-lanes.md).

struct.name: DCBDATA1
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_DCBDATA1
struct.doc: Display bus data, least significant word.

struct.name: SMASK1X
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK1X
struct.doc: Screen mask 1 x extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: SMASK1Y
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK1Y
struct.doc: Screen mask 1 y extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK2X
struct.doc: Screen mask 2 x extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: SMASK2Y
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK2Y
struct.doc: Screen mask 2 y extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: SMASK3X
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK3X
struct.doc: Screen mask 3 x extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: SMASK3Y
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK3Y
struct.doc: Screen mask 3 y extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: SMASK4X
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK4X
struct.doc: Screen mask 4 x extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: SMASK4Y
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_SMASK4Y
struct.doc: Screen mask 4 y extent, a minimum and a maximum packed in one word (NetBSD's comment: min and max, 16.16). Enabled through CLIPMODE.

struct.name: TOPSCAN
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_TOPSCAN; NetBSD sgimips Newport driver writes 0x3ff
struct.doc: Top-of-screen scanline. NetBSD's console init stores 0x3ff here with a comment that it does not know why; the meaning is read from the name only.

struct.name: XYWIN
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_XYWIN; NetBSD sgimips Newport driver writes (4096 << 16) | 4096
struct.doc: Window origin offset, x in bits 31:16 and y in bits 15:0 (inferred from NetBSD's console init, which stores 4096 in both halves). Linux declares it unnamed in role.

struct.name: CLIPMODE
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_CLIPMODE, REX3_CLIPMODE_*; Linux NPORT_CMODE_*
struct.doc: Clipping mode: one enable per screen mask (0 to 4) in bits 4:0 and four window-id match enables in bits 12:9. NetBSD stores a value at init that sets exactly the four match enables. Bits 8:5 are unnamed in both headers.

struct.name: STALL1
struct.from: NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_STALL1; Linux Newport framebuffer header leaves the word undeclared
struct.doc: NetBSD names this word a stall register, matching STALL0. Role inferred from the name; neither driver writes it.

struct.name: CONFIG
struct.from: NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_CONFIG (name and offset); Linux Newport framebuffer header struct newport_cregs and NPORT_CFG_* (bit layout)
struct.doc: Configuration register. NetBSD names the offset; the bit groups are Linux's alone, and no reading of any of them exists, so every field is inferred as a position only and its role is unknown. The register grade is inferred for the same reason.

struct.name: STATUS
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs) and NetBSD sgimips Newport register header REX3_REG_STATUS, REX3_STATUS_*; Linux NPORT_STAT_*
struct.doc: Status. Drivers only read it, polling the busy bits and the FIFO levels before sending more work. NetBSD and Linux agree on the busy bits and on the graphics FIFO level mask; they differ by one bit on the back-end FIFO level.

struct.name: USTATUS
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member ustatus
struct.doc: Linux declares a second status word here. Single source; no reading of its bits. MAME's model returns the status word for it, which is a model, not evidence.

struct.name: DCBRESET
struct.from: Linux Newport framebuffer header (struct newport_rexregs or newport_cregs; offset from the declared layout, checked with offsetof), member dcbreset
struct.doc: Linux declares a display-bus reset word here. Single source; no driver writes it. Role inferred from the name only.
